discovery: Cooling, trapping and quantum control of molecules at ultracold temperatures

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

motivation: Molecules, with their vibrational and rotational structure and permanent dipole moments, long resisted the cooling methods that transformed atomic physics. The nominees overcame this barrier. Jun Ye produced the first near-degenerate gases of ground-state polar molecules and demonstrated dipolar interactions and chemical reactions controlled at the quantum level. John Doyle invented buffer-gas cooling and, with collaborators, achieved direct laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of molecules, extending it to polyatomic species and optical tweezer arrays. David DeMille demonstrated the first laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of a diatomic molecule and used molecular precision measurements (ACME) to set the most stringent limits on the electron electric dipole moment, probing physics beyond the Standard Model. Together, their work created a new field: ultracold chemistry, molecular quantum simulation and computation, and tabletop tests of fundamental symmetries. The impact on atomic, molecular and particle physics is broad and lasting.
